author: J. G. Lucas
title: Angie Craig addresses federal policy changes and local collaboration in recent posts
text:
U.S. Representative Angie Craig, who has represented Minnesota’s 2nd district since 2019, posted a series of statements on March 24, 2026, addressing federal policy and local issues.
In a post published at 16:41 UTC, Craig criticized former President Donald Trump’s legislative agenda, writing “Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill was a slap in the face to Minnesotans. As if cutting nearly $200B in food assistance wasn’t cruel enough, Republicans also used it to create a $75B slush fund for Trump’s rogue ICE. I’ve got a bill to repeal ICE funding, restore SNAP and put”.
Later that day at 20:55 UTC, Craig highlighted her meeting with Woodbury Mayor Anne Burt: “Today, I met with Woodbury Mayor Anne Burt to discuss how we can bring federal funding back to Minnesota’s Second District and work together to make Woodbury an even better place to live and work. Thanks for stopping by, Mayor Burt! https://t.co/QQJOYj5EI4”.
At 22:22 UTC on the same day, Craig addressed the role of technology companies in child safety and legal accountability: “Time and time again, Big Tech has tried to pass off responsibility for their own negligence — and our kids have paid the price. Today, the courts agreed. The curtain is closing on Meta and Mark Zuckerberg’s charades. It’s past time to hold social media companies accountable for”.
Craig has served as U.S. Representative for Minnesota’s 2nd District since replacing Jason Lewis in 2019. She was born in West Helena, Arkansas in 1972 and currently resides in Prior Lake. Craig earned her BA from the University of Memphis in 1994.
